updates.summary: People keep it on the shelf for being "one of the most nocturnal films of all time," and that is the right kind of invitation. It is loose, funny, and quietly observant, like eavesdropping on five different late-night moods.
updates.good_pick_if: You want a conversational, low-stakes ensemble watch that drifts instead of rushes.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want one big plot or a film that builds toward a single payoff.

updates.summary: The cleanest pitch is that it plays as "pure romantic fantasia," where everyone is too stylish to stay mad for long. The dialogue snaps, the cast is stacked, and the whole thing runs on brittle charm.
updates.good_pick_if: You want sharp banter, immaculate cast chemistry, and classic rom-com timing.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want realism or a romance that feels less polished and performative.

updates.summary: The heart of it is the line that "poetry doesn't belong to those who write it; it belongs to those who need it," and the movie earns that tenderness. It is soft-spoken, romantic, and built around the pleasure of language finding a home.
updates.good_pick_if: You want a warm, low-conflict romance that treats language like a love language.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want sharper conflict, bigger laughs, or something less openly sentimental.

updates.summary: Its pull is that it puts "Falstaff as the narrative center" and lets Welles turn Shakespeare into something rougher, sadder, and more muscular. It feels old and alive at once, with battle, mischief, and melancholy all tangled together.
updates.good_pick_if: You want Shakespeare remade as a dense, character-first historical drama.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want a breezier adaptation or something less dense with names and dynastic baggage.

updates.summary: People talk about its "most thematically devastating" streak because Ozu sneaks adult disappointment into a kid's-eye comedy. It starts light, then leaves you with something much sadder about growing up.
updates.good_pick_if: You want quiet, patient comedy-drama with a real emotional aftertaste.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want momentum, spectacle, or a more obvious dramatic engine.

updates.summary: It is basically a "balls to the wall masterpiece" of greed, salesmanship, and self-destruction, which is why it plays so big in a group. Scorsese keeps the tempo ferocious enough that the satire feels like a sugar rush.
updates.good_pick_if: You want a loud, maximalist crowd watch with outrageous energy and no patience for restraint.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want moral subtlety, quiet character study, or a movie that is easy to sit through soberly.

updates.summary: People keep coming back because it is "one of the funniest, silliest & craziest films of all time," and the joke density is still absurd. It is sharp satire, but it never stops being a bright, stupid, very deliberate blast.
updates.good_pick_if: You want a quotable comedy that hits fast, keeps swinging, and actually has a brain.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want gentler humor or do not want the room to get irreverent.

updates.summary: The hook is that it is a "weirdly comforting nightmare," which is exactly the balance Obayashi strikes. It is chaotic, colorful, and so unhinged that it loops back around to being fun.
updates.good_pick_if: You want horror that behaves like a fever dream and still feels playful.
updates.maybe_skip_if: You want coherent logic, clean suspense, or a movie that stays in one tone.
